title: PyroNav MQTT sensor reading
description: One reading from one sensor. Owner: Member 1 (MQTT ingestion + 3D hospital). Publishers: the 3D hospital app (hospital-3d/), the virtual sensor simulator and real devices. Consumers: backend/sensor_ingestion (stores the reading and forwards it to the Decision Engine as the in-process event 'sensor_reading_received'), or any service that subscribes to the topic directly.

rules: The {room_id} and {sensor_id} topic levels MUST equal the payload's room_id and sensor_id; ingestion marks a mismatch as invalid.
sensor_id must be registered in the sensors table and belong to room_id (see hospital-3d-sensors.json and sample-sensors.json).
values holds every measurement the device reports in this message; a smoke_heat detector sends smoke AND temperature.
message_id is the idempotency key (sensor_readings.message_id is UNIQUE): a QoS 1 redelivery with the same id is stored and forwarded once.
timestamp is UTC. Readings older than INGESTION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 300 s) or more than 60 s in the future are stored as 'stale' and not forwarded to the Decision Engine.

informative_topics.pyronav/v1/clients/{client_id}/status: Retained {"status": "online"|"offline"} published by hospital-3d (MQTT last will). Not consumed by the backend.

message_id.description: Unique per message. hospital-3d uses 'h3d-<uuid>'. If omitted, ingestion derives one from sensor_id + timestamp.

sensor_type.description: Same enum as hazard-levels.json → sensor_type and the sensor_type_enum database type.

values.description: Measurement name → number. Field names per sensor_type: smoke_heat → smoke, temperature; co → co; current → current.

trigger.description: Why it was sent: slider | manual | periodic | reset | sync | test

x-forwarded-event._doc: After validation and storage, backend/sensor_ingestion publishes this on the in-process event bus. Member 2's Decision Engine subscribes with event_bus.subscribe(ev.SENSOR_READING_RECEIVED, handler). The WebSocket broadcaster forwards it to browsers as 'sensor_reading_updated' (see websocket-events.json).

data.persisted: boolean — false when PostgreSQL was unreachable; the reading is still forwarded in real time
